key_insight: A large randomized controlled trial at ICLR 2025 shows that LLM-generated feedback makes peer reviews measurably more informative and increases reviewer–author engagement.
problem_solved: Inconsistent, often unhelpful peer reviews and reviewer burden that slow paper improvement and author engagement; lack of scalable, practical interventions to raise review quality.
method: Large-scale randomized controlled trial: reviewers assigned to receive LLM-generated feedback versus control during the ICLR 2025 review process.
LLM-produced suggestions were integrated into reviewers' workflows and compared on outcomes such as review informativeness, length, and subsequent reviewer–author interaction.
Statistical analyses evaluated effect sizes and robustness across reviewer experience levels and paper types.
impact: Demonstrates that LLMs can augment human reviewers to improve review quality and stimulate constructive dialogue, offering a scalable tool to accelerate peer-review cycles and improve paper revisions.
visual_elements: RCT flow diagram: random assignment of reviewers → LLM feedback vs control → measured outcomes

paper_title: A large-scale randomized study of large language model feedback in peer review
paper_authors: Nitya Thakkar, Mert Yuksekgonul, Jake Silberg, Animesh Garg, Nanyun Peng
